title: GPU skyline memory advisor: per-request fingerprinting and soft-headroom for weights/KV/activations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a tighter, workload-aware GPU memory budgeting layer that can predict short-term 'skyline' usage across weights, KV cache, and activations at per-request granularity, then expose soft headroom recommendations to the scheduler and admission controller. Current heuristics (static margins + simple headroom percentages) are either too conservative (wasting capacity) or too brittle under mixed-precision, heterogeneous models, and bursty interactive traffic.

Goal: Build a lightweight 'skyline memory advisor' service that computes a per-tenant and per-request memory fingerprint, projects short-term memory skyline (99th percentile over a configurable horizon), and returns a soft-headroom target and suggested admission controls (e.g., delay, preemptible slot, fallback to quantized variant). The advisor integrates with continuous-batching controller and KV manager so decisions account for KV reuse and prefix cache hit probability.

Scope: MVP will include: (1) a compact per-request fingerprint vector (model size, seq_len, decoding-mode, kv-resident-bytes-est), (2) a streaming estimator that maintains a sliding quantile skyline per GPU pool and per-tenant, (3) an API for the scheduler/packing layer to request headroom advice, and (4) telemetry and knobs for tuning soft limits and fail-open behavior.

Out of scope for MVP: full RL-based admission policy, cross-region balancing, and auto-quantization rollouts (these are future items).
acceptance_criteria: Advisor exposes HTTP/gRPC endpoint returning headroom bytes and suggested action for a given fingerprint within <= 5ms median latency
Estimator maintains sliding 95th/99th skyline metrics for weights/KV/activations per GPU pool and per-tenant, surfaced to Console

Scheduler integrated with advisor will be able to apply suggested soft delays or route to quantized variants in synthetic benchmark showing >= 12% increase in successful admissions vs static-margins under bursty traffic
End-to-end tests covering hot-KV-hit and cold-KV scenarios with mixed precision models (fp16/int8) and sequence lengths up to 4096
Monitoring dashboards and alerts added: advisor-latency, skyline-variance, headroom-breaches, and action-applied-rate
notes: Related work: ENG-314159 (provisional safety ledger), ENG-842710 (memory-compass tiling) — advisor should read their ledgers as a data source

Trade-offs discussed in design review: prefer deterministic sliding-window quantiles for predictability vs heavier probabilistic forecasting. We chose lightweight quantile-merge to minimize overhead in runtime hot path.
Privacy: advisor stores only aggregated kernel-level telemetry and per-request compact fingerprints (no customer prompts).
